title: Inside the Milky Way
objective: After this level you can describe the Milky Way’s disk, spiral arms, central bulge and halo.
summary: The Milky Way has a bulge, a disk with arms and a halo. The Sun sits 26,000 light-years out and circles every 230 million years.

cards.headline: The Sun has circled the Milky Way only about 20 times since it formed.
The anatomy of a galaxy
cards.body: The Milky Way has a central bulge of stars, a flat disk about 100,000 light-years across with spiral arms, and a surrounding halo of old stars and globular star clusters. At the very center sits Sagittarius A*.

cards.headline: Our place in it
cards.body: The Sun lies about 26,000 light-years from the center, in a minor spiral arm. It orbits the galactic center too, taking about 230 million years for one lap, a “galactic year.” Since the Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago, it has made only about 20 laps.

cards.headline: Our galaxy: mapped
learned: The Milky Way has a bulge, a disk with arms, and a halo
The Sun is ~26,000 light-years from the center
One galactic orbit takes ~230 million years
Sagittarius A* sits at the center

questions.prompt: How long does the Sun take to orbit the center of the Milky Way?

options.label: About 13.8 billion years
options.rationale: That’s the age of the universe.

questions.explanation: The Sun takes about 230 million years to circle the Milky Way’s center once.

questions.prompt: Where is the Sun located in the Milky Way?

options.label: At the exact center, near Sagittarius A*
options.rationale: The center is about 26,000 light-years away.

options.label: In the disk, about 26,000 light-years from the center
In the halo, far above the disk
options.rationale: The Sun is in the disk.

options.label: At the outer edge of the galaxy

questions.explanation: The Sun sits in the disk, in a minor spiral arm, about 26,000 light-years from the galactic center.

questions.prompt: From Level 75: what sits at the very center of the Milky Way’s bulge?

options.label: A giant red star
options.rationale: The center holds something far more massive.

options.label: A second, smaller galaxy
options.rationale: The center is a single object.

options.label: A supermassive black hole, Sagittarius A*

questions.explanation: At the galaxy’s heart is Sagittarius A*, a black hole of about 4 million solar masses.
